casio-classwiz: Press [SHIFT] [MENU] (SETUP)
Press [2] (Angle Unit), then [1] (Degree)
Check that the D indicator shows at the top of the screen
ti-30xs: Press [mode]
On the top row, move the cursor to DEG and press [enter]
Press [clear] to return to the home screen; DEG shows at the top

standard-form-entry.title: Enter a number in standard form

casio-classwiz: Type {mantissa}, press [×10ˣ], then type {power} (press [(−)] first if the power is negative) (check on your model)
Or type {mantissa} [×] 10 [xⁿ] {power} [►], which works on every model
Put brackets round each standard-form number when you divide by it
ti-30xs: Type {mantissa}, press [×10ⁿ], then type {power} (press [(−)] first if the power is negative)
Press [►] to leave the power
Put brackets round each standard-form number when you divide by it

standard-form-reading.title: Show and read an answer in standard form

casio-classwiz: Press [SHIFT] [MENU] (SETUP) [3] (Number Format) [2] (Sci), then [3] for 3 significant figures
Press [=]: a display of 1.67×10⁻¹ means 1.67 × 10⁻¹
To go back to normal display: [SHIFT] [MENU] (SETUP) [3] (Number Format) [3] (Norm) [1] (Norm 1)
ti-30xs: Press [mode], press [▼] to the NORM SCI ENG row, move to SCI and press [enter]
Press [clear], then calculate: a display of 5×10⁻³ means 5 × 10⁻³
To go back: [mode], [▼] to the second row, choose NORM and press [enter]

casio-classwiz: Press [■/■] for the fraction template
Type {numerator}, press [▼], type {denominator}
Press [►] to leave the fraction, then carry on
ti-30xs: Press [n/d] for the fraction template
Type {numerator}, press [▼], type {denominator}
Press [►] to leave the fraction, then carry on

fraction-to-decimal.title: Switch an answer between fraction and decimal

casio-classwiz: After [=], press [S⇔D] to switch between the fraction (or √, π form) and the decimal
Or press [SHIFT] [=] (≈) instead of [=] to get the decimal straight away
ti-30xs: After [enter], press the toggle key [◄►] to switch between the fraction (or √, π form) and the decimal
Or end the entry with [2nd] [f◄►d] before [enter] to convert to a decimal

mixed-numbers.title: Enter a mixed number and convert the answer

casio-classwiz: Press [SHIFT] [■/■] (■□/□) for the mixed-number template
Type {whole}, press [►], type {numerator}, press [▼], type {denominator}, press [►]
Press [=]; to switch the answer between mixed and improper form, press [SHIFT] [S⇔D] (a b/c ⇔ d/c)
ti-30xs: Type {whole}, then press [2nd] [Un/d]
Type {numerator}, press [▼], type {denominator}, press [►]
For a mixed-number answer, end the entry with [2nd] [n/d◄►Un/d] before [enter]

casio-classwiz: Square: type {base}, press [x²]
Any power: type {base}, press [xⁿ], type {power}, press [►]
Negative power: press [(−)] before the power, e.g. {base} [xⁿ] [(−)] {power} [►]
Put a negative base in brackets: [(] [(−)] {base} [)] [x²]
ti-30xs: Square: type {base}, press [x²]
Any power: type {base}, press [^], type {power}, press [►]
Negative power: press [(−)] before the power, e.g. {base} [^] [(−)] {power} [►]
Put a negative base in brackets: [(] [(−)] {base} [)] [x²]

roots.title: Square roots, cube roots and other roots

casio-classwiz: Square root: press [√■], type {value}, press [►]
Cube root: press [SHIFT] [√■] (∛■), type {value}, press [►] (fx-991EX: check on your model)
Any root: press [SHIFT] [xⁿ] (■√□), type {root}, press [►], type {value}, press [►]
ti-30xs: Square root: press [2nd] [√], type {value}; press [►] to leave the root before carrying on
Cube root or any root: type {root}, press [2nd] [ˣ√], then type {value}
Press [enter]

casio-classwiz: Type {base} and press [xⁿ]
In the power box type {numerator}, press [■/■], type {denominator}
Press [=]
ti-30xs: Type {base} and press [^]
Type the power in brackets: [(] {numerator} [÷] {denominator} [)]
Press [enter]

casio-classwiz: Type {value}, press [x⁻¹], press [=]
For the reciprocal of a calculation, put it in brackets first: [(] … [)] [x⁻¹]
ti-30xs: Type {value}, press [x⁻¹], press [enter]
For the reciprocal of a calculation, put it in brackets first: [(] … [)] [x⁻¹]

casio-classwiz: The calculator follows the order of operations: brackets, then powers, then × and ÷, then + and −
Put a whole numerator or denominator in brackets, e.g. [(] … [)] [÷] [(] … [)]
Close the bracket after a function's input, e.g. [sin] 30 [)]
Square a negative number in brackets: [(] [(−)] 2 [)] [x²] gives 4; [(−)] 2 [x²] gives −4
ti-30xs: The calculator follows the order of operations: brackets, then powers, then × and ÷, then + and −
Put a whole numerator or denominator in brackets, e.g. [(] … [)] [÷] [(] … [)]
Close the bracket after a function's input, e.g. [sin] 30 [)]
Square a negative number in brackets: [(] [(−)] 2 [)] [x²] gives 4; [(−)] 2 [x²] gives −4

casio-classwiz: Press [SHIFT] [×10ˣ] (π) wherever π appears
Example: [SHIFT] [×10ˣ] (π) [×] {radius} [x²] [=], then [S⇔D] for the decimal
ti-30xs: Press [π] wherever π appears
Example: [π] [×] {radius} [x²] [enter], then [◄►] for the decimal

trig.title: sin, cos and tan of an angle

casio-classwiz: Check the calculator is in degrees (D at the top)
Press [sin], [cos] or [tan], type {angle}, press [)]
Press [=]; for a decimal, press [S⇔D] or use [SHIFT] [=] (≈)
ti-30xs: Check the calculator is in degrees (DEG at the top)
Press [sin], [cos] or [tan], type {angle}, press [)]
Press [enter]; for a decimal, press [◄►]

inverse-trig.title: Find an angle with sin⁻¹, cos⁻¹ or tan⁻¹

casio-classwiz: Check the calculator is in degrees (D at the top)
Press [SHIFT] [sin] (sin⁻¹), [SHIFT] [cos] (cos⁻¹) or [SHIFT] [tan] (tan⁻¹)
Type {ratio}, using [■/■] for a fraction, then press [)] [=]
ti-30xs: Check the calculator is in degrees (DEG at the top)
Press [2nd] [sin⁻¹], [2nd] [cos⁻¹] or [2nd] [tan⁻¹]
Type {ratio}, using [n/d] for a fraction, then press [)] [enter]

casio-classwiz: Press [Ans] to put the last answer into a calculation
Start with an operation key, e.g. [÷] 7 [=], and the calculator uses Ans automatically
Ans keeps every digit, so use it instead of retyping a rounded value
ti-30xs: Press [2nd] [answer] to put the last answer into a calculation
Start with an operation key, e.g. [÷] 7 [enter], and the calculator uses Ans automatically
Ans keeps every digit, so use it instead of retyping a rounded value

casio-classwiz: Turn on the frequency column first: [SHIFT] [MENU] (SETUP) [▼], then [3] (Statistics) on the fx-991EX or [1] (Statistics) on the fx-83GTX / fx-85GTX, then [1] (On)
Press [MENU], highlight the Statistics icon (fx-83GTX / fx-85GTX: icon 2) and press [=], then [1] (1-Variable)
Type each value and press [=] after it, going down the x column
Press [▼] [►] to reach the top of the Freq column (the guide's sequence; check on your model), then type each frequency and press [=] after it
Press [AC], then [OPTN] [▼] [2] (Variable) [1] (x̄) [=]
ti-30xs: Clear old data: press [data] [data], press [▼] three times to 4: Clear ALL, press [enter]
In L1, type each value and press [▼] after it
Press [►] to move to L2, then type each frequency and press [▼] after it
Press [2nd] [stat] [1] (1-Var Stats); press [▼], then [►] [►] to set FRQ to L2, and press [enter] [enter]
Read x̄ on line 2 of the results

casio-classwiz: Work out the midpoint of each class by hand: (lower bound + upper bound) ÷ 2
Follow the frequency-table mean steps with the midpoints as the x values and the class frequencies in the Freq column
Say the answer is an estimate: the midpoints stand in for the real values
ti-30xs: Work out the midpoint of each class by hand: (lower bound + upper bound) ÷ 2
Follow the frequency-table mean steps with the midpoints in L1 and the class frequencies in L2
Say the answer is an estimate: the midpoints stand in for the real values

stats-mode-exit.title: Go back to normal calculations after statistics

casio-classwiz: Press [MENU], highlight the Calculate icon (icon 1) and press [=]
Leaving Statistics mode deletes the data in the editor
ti-30xs: Press [2nd] [quit] to return to the home screen
Clear the old lists before the next data set: [data] [data], then 4: Clear ALL

time-dms.title: Times in hours, minutes and seconds

casio-classwiz: Enter a time as {hours} [°'"] {minutes} [°'"] {seconds} [°'"] (type 0 for any part that is zero)
Add or subtract times the same way, then press [=]: the answer shows as hours° minutes' seconds"
Press [°'"] on an answer to switch between hours-minutes-seconds and decimal hours
ti-30xs: Enter a time as {hours} [2nd] [angle] [1] (°), {minutes} [2nd] [angle] [2] ('), {seconds} [2nd] [angle] [3] (")
Add or subtract times the same way, then press [enter]: the answer shows in decimal hours
To see hours-minutes-seconds, press [2nd] [angle] [6] (►DMS) [enter]

compound-interest.title: Compound interest and repeated percentage change

casio-classwiz: Press [xⁿ], type {years}, press [=]
For a decrease use [−] instead of [+]; round only the final answer
ti-30xs: Press [^], type {years}, press [enter]
For a decrease use [−] instead of [+]; round only the final answer

casio-classwiz: Best: write down the full display, then round it by hand to {sf} significant figures
Or set Sci: [SHIFT] [MENU] (SETUP) [3] (Number Format) [2] (Sci), then [{sf}]; the answer shows as a × 10ⁿ rounded to {sf} significant figures
Turn it off afterwards: [SHIFT] [MENU] (SETUP) [3] (Number Format) [3] (Norm) [1] (Norm 1)
ti-30xs: Best: write down the full display, then round it by hand to {sf} significant figures
Or press [mode], choose SCI on row 2, and on row 3 choose the digit one less than {sf}; the answer shows as a × 10ⁿ (check on your model)
Turn it off afterwards: [mode], choose NORM and FLOAT

casio-classwiz: Set Fix: [SHIFT] [MENU] (SETUP) [3] (Number Format) [1] (Fix), then [{dp}]
Answers now show rounded to {dp} decimal places; the calculator still keeps every digit
Turn it off afterwards: [SHIFT] [MENU] (SETUP) [3] (Number Format) [3] (Norm) [1] (Norm 1)
ti-30xs: Press [mode], press [▼] [▼] to the FLOAT 0123456789 row, move to {dp} and press [enter]
Press [clear]; answers now show rounded to {dp} decimal places
Turn it off afterwards: [mode], [▼] [▼], choose FLOAT and press [enter]

casio-classwiz: Type [(] {new} [−] {original} [)] [÷] {original}
Press [SHIFT] [Ans] (%) [=] to get the change as a percentage
A negative answer is a percentage decrease
ti-30xs: Type [(] {new} [−] {original} [)] [÷] {original} [×] 100
Press [enter] to get the change as a percentage
A negative answer is a percentage decrease

casio-classwiz: Type {amount} [×] {percent}
Press [SHIFT] [Ans] (%) [=]
ti-30xs: Type {percent}, press [2nd] [%]
Press [×], type {amount}, press [enter]
